entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 30.10.2015 passed by 5th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur (C.G.), in Claim Case No.16/2014 awarding compensation of Rs.12,36,600/- with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the claimants for their irreparable loss.
2.

entities.text: 5th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The gist of claim before the Claims Tribunal, in brief, was that on 11.10.2013 while deceased Rajkumar Donde along with his friend Toman Sahu was going from Simga to his village Farfaud on his motorcycle, respondent no.6 Keshav Ram Patel driving the offending vehicle i.e. Tractor bearing registration No.CG 04 DT 8828 rashly and negligently dashed his motorcycle, as a result of which,
Rajkumar Donde suffered grievous injuries and died on the spot.

The matter was reported to Police Station, Kharora, Raipur thereon a criminal case was registered against the driver and charge sheet was filed in the concerned Court.
3.
It is claimed that at the time of accident, the age of the deceased was about 28 years who was a carpenter by profession and was earning Rs.2,50,000/- per annum by making furniture.
Due to the casual death of deceased Rajkumar Donde, there is an irreparable loss to the claimants who are the wife, daughter, sister and parents of the deceased.
Therefore, the claimants had preferred an application before the Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs. 31,50,000/-.

4. Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record, assessed the income of the deceased to be Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19840 Rs.4,500/- per month i.e.
54,000/- per annum.
Since the deceased was aged about 28 years, 50% of the income was added towards future prospects, making the amount Rs.81,000/-.

Further, considering the age of the deceased and the fact that the claimants are the wife, daughter, sister and parents of the deceased,
1/5th of the income was deducted towards personal expenses and after deduction, the amount comes to Rs.64,800/-.
Considering the age of the deceased, multiplier of 17 was applied and the total loss of dependency worked out to Rs. 11,01,600/-.
Further, Rs.25,000/- for spousal consortium, Rs.80,000 for love and affection, Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.20,000 for physical and mental agony has been awarded.

Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.12,36,600/- in favour of the claimants with interest @ 9% per annum,
from the date of application till its realization.
Hence, this appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company challenging the impugned award.
5. It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company that the Tribunal has granted 50% of the income towards future prospects which is excessive.
He submits that considering the age of the deceased and the fact that he did not have any regular income as he was working as a carpenter it should have been 40%.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in favour of the Claimants is excessive and the same needs to be modified suitably.
6. There is no representation on behalf of the respondents.

7. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In a motor accident claim case, what is important is that, the compensation to be awarded by the Courts/Tribunals should be just and proper compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.

It should neither be a meager amount of compensation Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19840 nor a Bonanza.
9.
Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
10. The main contention of the Insurance Company is that 50% of the income awarded by the Tribunal towards future prospects is excessive.

Considering the age of the deceased to be 28 years at the time of incident and in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, future prospects should be 40% instead of 50% as has been wrongly held by the Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. However, the Tribunal in para-16 of its award has held that the claimants has brought on record Ex.P-8 showing that the deceased had received carpentry training by participating in carpentry training program conducted by Rural Development and Self-Employment Training Institute.

entities.text: Rural Development and Self-Employment Training Institute
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Perusal of the evidence it is evident that the deceased was a carpenter by profession.
Hence, he would fall under the category of skilled labour.

The deceased met with accident on 11.10.2013 and as per the notification by Labour Department, the minimum wages of a skilled labour at that point of time was Rs.5605 per month i.e. Rs.67,260 per annum.
Even if 40% of the income i.e. Rs.26904 is added towards future prospects, the amount comes to Rs.94,164/-.

In the present case, in total,
there are five claimants, so the deduction of 1/5th of the income towards personal expenses held by the Tribunal is proper and after deduction, the amount comes to Rs.75331.2.
Similarly, the age of the deceased was 28 years, so the multiplier of 17 applied by the Tribunal is proper and applying the said multiplier the total loss of dependency works out to Rs.12,00,630.4.

In addition, the claimants would also be entitled for Rs.15,000/-
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19840 towards loss of estate and Rs. 15,000/- for funeral expenses.

As per 'Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu, reported in AIR Online 2018 SC 189, the claimants are further entitled for Rs. 40,000/- each towards loss of consortium and love and affection totaling Rs. 2,00,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu, reported in AIR Online 2018 SC 189
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In this situation, the argument of the Insurance Company, that the Tribunal, by accepting 50% of the income towards future prospects, has calculated and awarded excessive compensation in favour of the claimants, is not acceptable.
13. Accordingly, this appeal of the Insurance Company is hereby dismissed.

Sd/-
